message.content:
Order filled at $223.00.

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and checked the live quote ($222.70 last, $222.68/$222.72 bid/ask) before buying. The filing showed a business with improving operating quality despite modest top-line growth: net sales of $391,035M (+2% YoY), gross margin of $180,683M (46.2%, up from 44.1%), operating income of $123,216M (+7.8%), operating cash flow of $118,254M, and diluted EPS of $6.08, with Services revenue of $96,169M (+13%) at 73.9% gross margin carrying the margin expansion. Net income was $93,736M, down from $96,995M, but only because of a one-time $10.2B net tax charge from the EC State Aid Decision — pretax income actually rose to $123,485M, so the decline is non-operating rather than a deterioration in the franchise. Note that the filing's "Highlights" line and its Statements of Operations both misstate FY2024 net income as $96,995M, which is the prior year's figure and inconsistent with the $6.08 diluted EPS and the $93,736M reported in the comprehensive income, equity, and cash flow statements; I used $93,736M. I weighed that against the real risks disclosed — Greater China net sales down 8% to $66,952M, DOJ monopolization litigation, EU DMA noncompliance proceedings with fines of up to 10% of worldwide net sales, and heavy supply-chain concentration — and concluded a modest position was warranted rather than a full-size one. I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares of AAPL at $223.00, which filled at $223.00 for $9,812 total — within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, inside the AAPL/MSFT-only universe, and with a limit about 0.13% above the ask so it was close to market. No funds were moved out of the account, and I left the existing 100 MSFT shares untouched.
